column1: Save reusable Schema Compare configuration in an {{c1::.scmp}} file.
column2:
An .scmp file saves what to compare and which differences to report. Reopen it for a repeatable comparison instead of manually selecting the endpoints and exclusions each time.
Review source

column1: To skip formatting-only differences in Schema Compare, enable {{c1::Ignore whitespace}}.
column2:
Ignore whitespace prevents an indentation or spacing change from showing up as a difference. It does not ignore a change to an actual SQL expression. Keep the setting consistent across runs.
Review source

column1: If only the positions of columns changed and those positions do not matter, enable {{c1::Ignore column order}} in Schema Compare.
column2:
Ignore column order prevents changed positions alone from appearing as drift. Leave it off when a consumer depends on column positions, such as code that reads SELECT * by ordinal.
Review source

column1: SqlPackage's broad option for dropping target-only objects defaults to {{c1::DropObjectsNotInSource=False}}.
column2:
The broad setting does not drop target-only objects by default. Separate settings can still remove specific types, such as indexes under DropIndexesNotInSource. Read the plan before you publish.
Review source

column1: SqlPackage's default guard against schema changes that can lose data is {{c1::BlockOnPossibleDataLoss=True}}.
column2:
The guard can block a change based on the risk in the schema operation, even when the target table is empty. It is not a guarantee against every deployment side effect.
Review source

column1: To copy the current definitions from a live database into an output file or folder, use SqlPackage {{c1::/Action:Extract}}.
column2:
Extract reads the database as it is now and writes a snapshot of its definitions. Use a separate output location so you can compare it with the maintained project without replacing source files.
Review source

column1: During SqlPackage Extract, {{c1::/p:ExtractTarget=SchemaObjectType}} organizes SQL files by schema and object type.
column2:
SchemaObjectType places individual SQL files into a layout grouped by schema and object type. Choose SqlProject instead if you also need a generated project file.
Review source

column1: To extract both a .sqlproj and individual object definitions, use {{c1::/p:ExtractTarget=SqlProject}}.
column2:
SqlProject creates a project file along with the object definitions and database options. Inspect the result before adopting it as source. Extraction reflects the live database, including unintended changes.
Review source

column1: When previewing how the project would change production, set the live database as Schema Compare's {{c1::target}}.
column2:
Schema Compare proposes changes to the target, using the source as the desired state. Reverse the direction only when you want to bring a live change into the project.
Review source

column1: Install prerelease DacpacVerify globally with {{c1::dotnet tool install --global Microsoft.DacpacVerify --prerelease}}.
column2:
The prerelease switch lets the .NET CLI choose a prerelease package. Run dacpacverify with the before and after packages. It compares package content, including deployment scripts.
